title: Showcase
subtitle: Ten weeks that were not ten separate topics. Here is the shape they made.
objectives: Trace the arc across the ten themes of the term
Choose a passage and say why it mattered
Explain a belief without performing it
Name one habit that changed this term
Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

cards.title: Ten weeks, and they were in an order
cards.text: Foundations first, then trust, faith, love, prayer. Then worship, perseverance, honesty, humility, courage.

cards.title: Ten weeks, one tap each
cards.text: This is your revision sheet. The second line of each is the thing most often got wrong.

cards.title: Belief first, then what it costs
cards.text: The first half was about what you hold. The second half was about what holding it asks of you when it is expensive.
points: **Weeks 1 to 5:** foundation, trust, faith, love, prayer.
**Weeks 6 to 10:** worship, trials, honesty, humility, courage.
**The second half is the first half tested.**

question.text: What did the second half of the term mostly deal with?
options: What belief costs when it is tested
question.explain: Worship, perseverance, honesty, humility and courage are all the first half under pressure.

cards.title: Everything gets tested eventually
cards.text: You can drill a combination perfectly on pads and lose it in the first round. Nobody knows it holds until it is under pressure.
points: **Untested is not the same as strong.**

cards.title: Pick one and be able to say why
cards.text: A showcase usually asks you to choose. The choice matters less than being able to explain it clearly.
points: **Name the passage** and roughly where it is.

question.text: James 1:2 asks you to feel happy about difficulties.
question.explain: 'Consider' is a thinking word. It asks for a judgement about how to read a situation, not a feeling.

cards.title: Good place to pause
cards.text: Part 2 is how to talk about it, and one habit. Then a review of the whole term.

cards.title: The week 9 problem, in a showcase
cards.text: Matthew 6 warns about doing things to be seen. A showcase asks you to be seen. Both of those are true at once.

cards.title: Explaining is not announcing
cards.text: Saying what a passage means and saying how well you follow it are different things. The first is the task here.
points: **Explain the text**, not your record with it.
**Do not claim what you have not done.**

cards.title: Every good example this term named the cost
cards.text: 'Even if he does not.' 'If I perish, I perish.' 'We cannot help speaking.' The line comes first, every time.
points: **A character who never counts it** is not brave.
**Look for the sentence.** It is always there.

cards.title: Name the thing that actually changed
cards.text: Not what you agree with. What is different in an ordinary week because of something in these ten lessons.
points: **Small and real** beats large and stated.
**It is a better one than an invented change.**

question.text: What is the honest thing to do in a showcase if nothing has changed yet?
options: Say so, and say what you found hardest
Describe a change you have not made
question.explain: Week 8's whole argument. An invented answer is the one thing the term argued against.

cards.title: Ten weeks is a short time
cards.text: Joseph waited years. Nobody is expecting a finished person at the end of a term. The direction is the point.

question.text: Courage, as this term defined it, means not feeling afraid.
question.explain: It means acting while afraid. Without the fear, the action is easy rather than brave.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **One real change** beats a stated one.

quiz.text: In the parable of the builders, what happens to the two houses?
options: Both face the same storm; only one stands
Only the foolish builder's house is rained on
quiz.explain: Week 1. That both face the same weather is stated, not implied.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the difference between the two builders?
options: One acted on the words; the other only heard them
One had never heard the words
quiz.explain: Week 1. Hearing and doing is the whole distinction.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the difference between trust and obedience?
options: Trust is what you believe; obedience is what you do about it
Trust is for adults and obedience for children
quiz.explain: Week 2. Proverbs 3:5-6 asks for one and 1 Samuel 15:22 for the other.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: In 1 Samuel 15, doing most of what was asked was treated as obedience.
quiz.explain: Week 2. Partial obedience is treated as disobedience, and the offering did not make up for it.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What does Hebrews 11:1 define?
quiz.explain: Week 3. Confidence in what is hoped for and assurance about what is not seen.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the point of the mustard seed image?
options: A very small amount of faith is enough
Faith grows only if you feed it
You need a great deal of faith
quiz.explain: Week 3. The smallness is deliberate. Size is not what the verse is about.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: How does 1 Corinthians 13 describe love?
options: As a list of behaviours rather than feelings
As a feeling you either have or do not
As a rule for priests only
quiz.explain: Week 4. It was written to a church that was arguing, which is why it reads as a checklist.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What does the new command in John 13:34-35 change?
options: The measure of love, from 'as yourself' to 'as I have loved you'
Which day is set aside for worship
quiz.explain: Week 4. It does not replace loving your neighbour; it raises the standard.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What does ACTS stand for in prayer?
quiz.explain: Week 5. Asking comes last, and the three before it change what you ask for.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: Philippians 4:6-7 promises that you will get what you ask for.
quiz.explain: Week 5. What it promises is peace guarding your heart and mind. That is a different promise.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What does Romans 12:1 call true and proper worship?
options: Offering your body as a living sacrifice
Giving a tenth of your income
quiz.explain: Week 6. A living sacrifice can walk away, so it has to be offered again.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What does John 4:24 require of worship?
quiz.explain: Week 6. Spirit without truth is feeling with no content; truth without spirit is facts with no heart.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What is the order of the chain in Romans 5:3-5?
quiz.explain: Week 7. Each one produces the next, and none of the links can be skipped.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What does perseverance require to count as perseverance?
quiz.explain: Week 7. If you cannot leave, staying is endurance rather than perseverance.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: How long did Joseph stay in prison after the cupbearer forgot him?
quiz.explain: Week 7. Genesis 41:1. The gap is written into the text deliberately.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What reason does Ephesians 4:25 give for honesty?
options: We are all members of one body
quiz.explain: Week 8. A lie damages something shared, so it is not a private act.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What were Ananias and Sapphira judged for?
options: Lying about how much they had given
quiz.explain: Week 8. Peter says the money was theirs. The claim was the offence, not the amount.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: If every word you say is true, it cannot be a lie.
quiz.explain: Week 8. Honesty is measured by what the other person ends up believing.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: Whose job was foot washing in a household?
quiz.explain: Week 9. That is why Peter objected rather than being merely embarrassed.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: Why did the widow's two coins count for more?
options: She gave everything she had, out of her poverty
quiz.explain: Week 9. The measure is what it cost the giver, not the size of the gift.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What is humility, as this term defined it?
options: Thinking about yourself less, rather than thinking badly of yourself
quiz.explain: Week 9. Someone who insults himself constantly is still talking about himself.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What did the three men in Daniel 3 say?
options: God is able to rescue us, but even if he does not, we will not bow
We will bow if we are not rescued
We will decide once we see what happens
quiz.explain: Week 10. Their answer did not depend on the outcome, which is what makes it courage.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What did Daniel do when praying was made illegal?
options: Carried on exactly as before, with the window open
quiz.explain: Week 10. He neither hid nor protested. The consistency was the statement.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

quiz.text: What does courage require?
quiz.explain: Week 10. Without the fear, the action is easy rather than brave.
quiz.objective: Recall the ten Devotion topics of the term

teacher.summary: Week 11 is the devotion showcase. The deck's main contribution is the arc: these were not ten unrelated themes, and naming the split — weeks 1 to 5 are what you hold, weeks 6 to 10 are what holding it costs — makes the term memorable as one shape rather than a list. The showcase itself raises a genuine tension the term already handled, since Matthew 6 warns about doing things to be seen and a showcase asks exactly that; the lesson resolves it by distinguishing explaining a passage from advertising your record with it. 'Nothing has changed yet' is explicitly offered as an honest answer, which is consistent with week 8 and matters more than a tidy one.
discussion: Ask him to describe the shape of the term in two sentences before looking at the figure.
Ask which passage he would choose, and make him give the reason in three sentences.
Ask what the difference is between explaining a text and advertising how well you follow it.
Ask what actually changed in an ordinary week. Accept 'nothing yet' without argument.
teacher.extension: Have him write the one sentence that names the cost, for a decision he is facing. Every example this term had one.
misconceptions: 'The ten weeks were separate topics.' The second half is the first half under pressure.
'A showcase means saying how well you are doing.' The task is explaining the text, not your record.
'Consider it pure joy means feel happy.' It is a judgement, not a feeling.
'Courage means not being afraid.' It means acting while afraid.
